source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items says `Encode: H.264`, while Procedure only says display video and inspect visual issues/bleeding edge, and Criteria is TBD. Encoding and display/decode are materially different pipelines, so an authoritative scope and oracle require Engineering Decision while Master stays unchanged.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Operation semantics and acceptance are not merely missing parameters: the source does not establish which media pipeline is being tested. Neither a package nor ordinary confirmation can make one path authoritative, so execution is BLOCKED pending ruling and fresh review.

engineering_decision_request.question: Resolve Functionality row 1780 Wistron-HW-00413-V002: whether authoritative H.264 coverage is GPU hardware encoding as stated by Items, decode/playback plus visual `bleeding edge` inspection as stated by Procedure, or separately accepted stages; define exact GPU/API/profile/input/output/frame/quality/visual criteria and recovery, preserve Master TBD, and require fresh review.

review_improvement: Exposes the encode-versus-display pipeline conflict, rejects CPU libx264 as GPU evidence and prevents undefined visual language or TBD criteria from being converted into an executable codec verdict.
independent_technical_reasoning: Hardware encode, decode and scanout have independent engines and failure signatures. A valid bitstream says nothing about physical edges, while a clean displayed reference says nothing about encoding. Without naming the stage and reference oracle, even technically correct ffmpeg commands can test the wrong subsystem and cannot support a verdict.
